To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the stability of DNA duplexes is characterized by positive changes in heat capacities; 2) the stability of duplexes containing the GG, AA and TT mismatches can be estimated using thermodynamic parameters derived for the corresponding duplexes containing the GC, AT and CC base pairs; 3) duplexes containing the CC mismatch exhibit a significantly higher stability than the duplexes containing other mismatches.

(i) all the DNA duplexes studied in our work exhibit positive DeltaC(p) values; (ii) none of the DNA duplexes exhibit two-state melting; (iii) the GG, AA and TT mismatches have a local impact on duplex stability, while the CC mismatch affects the stability of the entire helix.

the fundamental problem of the origin and nature of DNA duplex stability and the thermodynamics of DNA duplex melting.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the thermodynamics of DNA duplex melting is complex and depends on many factors, including the sequence context, the length of the oligomer, and the presence of mismatched base pairs.
the thermodynamic stability of duplex DNA is a complex function of many factors, and it is impossible to predict its behavior in a given situation without a detailed analysis.
all the mismatches studied in this work are destabilizing, and their destabilizing impact is not uniform.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stability of DNA duplexes is not only determined by the sequence composition of the helix but is also strongly influenced by the sequence composition in the flanking helical domains.
the thermodynamic stability of DNA duplexes depends on the sequence context and the nature of the central triplet, but the impact of a mismatch is confined to the central triplet.
, in addition to the sequence-dependent contributions, the thermodynamic stability of DNA duplexes is also affected by the nature of the mismatched pair.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stability of DNA duplexes with GG, CC, or AA mismatches is significantly higher than previously thought.
a mismatched DNA duplex may exhibit a two-state melting only if the mismatch is not too close to the ends of the duplex.
DNA duplexes that contain a single mismatch are not thermodynamically stable and that the stability of a duplex is a property of the entire duplex, not just of the mismatch site.
